scenes.text: One AI agent can plan a trip. [1] But what if you had a whole team of agents, a researcher, a writer and a checker, all working together? [2] Let's understand multi agent systems.

title: Multi-Agent
Systems
data.subtitle: AI agents working as a team

scenes.text: A multi agent system is a group of AI agents, each with its own role, all working toward one goal. [1] Think of it like a small company, but made of AI. [2] Each agent has a specialty, [3] they pass work to each other, [4] and a manager agent coordinates them.

data.definition: Several AI agents, each with its own role, working together toward one goal.

scenes.text: Say the goal is, write a report on electric scooters in India. [1] The manager agent breaks it into tasks. [2] A research agent searches the web for data. [3] A writer agent drafts the report. [4] A reviewer agent checks the facts and suggests fixes, [5] and the manager delivers the final report to you.

So why not just use one big agent? [1] One agent doing everything can get overloaded, and lose track on long tasks. [2] A team of focused agents keeps each job small and clear, and they can even work in parallel.

left.title: One agent
left.label: can lose track on big jobs

right.title: Agent team
right.label: smaller jobs, can run in parallel

scenes.text: Here are four common team patterns. [1] Manager and workers, where one boss hands out tasks. [2] Pipeline, where each agent passes work to the next, like an assembly line. [3] Debate, where agents argue different sides to reach a better answer. [4] And reviewer, where one agent checks another's work.

So where is this used? [1] In software, where one agent plans, another writes code, and another tests it. [2] In deep research tools, which send many agents to read sources at once. [3] And in customer support, where agents route, answer and escalate questions.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think more agents always means better results. [2] Not always. Every extra agent adds cost, delay, and more chances for mistakes to be passed along. Often, one good agent with the right tools is enough.

data.myth: More agents always means better results.
data.fact: Each agent adds cost, delay and more chances for mistakes. One good agent is often enough.
data.tip: Start simple, add agents if needed

scenes.text: Quick quiz! In a multi agent system, what does the manager agent usually do? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] It breaks the goal into tasks, and coordinates the team!

Let's recap. [1] A multi agent system is a team of agents with different roles. [2] A manager splits the goal and coordinates. [3] Teams keep jobs focused, and can work in parallel.
